title: Does a nailer's recoil slow a G1 down when it fires a whole 62-nail sheet in sequence?
summary: The 62 nails of a 4x8 sheet fired in serpentine order, each shot's recoil transient taken from 45 MuJoCo traces of the Menagerie G1 hold model (three hold heights, three loops, 0.25–4 N s). The next nail waits until the nosepiece is back on the wall and the tip is within 0.25–4 mm; the left-over error joins the robot scatter and the shared stud-finding error in one clean-sheet probability. The wait after a shot is 0 s at 0.25 N s and up to 0.25–0.31 s at 4 N s, set by the wall coming back, not by tip position; the shortest move between nails is 0.16 s at 0.5 m/s, so a sheet is slowed by 0 s, and by 2.3–2.5 s only for a 4 N s recoil with a 1–4 m/s, 10 m/s² tip. Left-over error is at most 0.37 mm, so the clean-sheet probability is unchanged (1.00 with perfect stud reads, 0.93 with a 1 mm read): the stud finder, not recoil, keeps the budget. The recoil, loop delay, tip speed and wall are swept, not sourced; the transient is not re-simulated along the sheet and re-stancing is not modelled.
lede: does a nailer's recoil slow a G1 down when it fires a whole 62-nail sheet in sequence? Not by much: the arm is settled and back on the wall within 0.31 s at 4 N s of recoil, shorter than the 0.16 s moves only for a fast tip, so a sheet loses 0 s (2.3-2.5 s at 10 m/s2 and 4 N s) and the clean-sheet probability does not move; the stud finder still sets the budget (recoil, loop, tip speed and wall are swept, not sourced).
